title: Siłownia · dobrych, dobrymi, dobrym
note:
C1 Block 2, unit 6 - THE PLURAL ADJECTIVE GYM (C1-SPINE O11). Gym idiom, the a1_case_gym / a2_case_gym2 / b1_case_gym / b1_virile_gym / b2_adj_gym / b2_plural_gym / b2_case_gym line: ZERO NEW MATERIAL, teaches_structures and teaches_lemmas both EMPTY. Every form here was taught by c1_adj_pl_gen [182], c1_adj_pl_loc [183], c1_adj_pl_inst [184], c1_adj_pl_dat [185], c1_adj_pl_virile [186], or by b2_loc_pl / b2_inst_pl / b2_dat_pl / b2_gen_pl_full / a2_gen_pl / a2_plural_nom for the nouns.

WHY THE SLOT IS EARNED, against AGENTS' gyms rule, which is binding and which retired a2_past_gym for failing exactly this test ('a repetition of things that were not difficult'). C1-SPINE O11 pre-authorised this gym and the argument holds up on inspection: three strings (-ych, -ymi, -ym) are spread across SIX jobs, and -ych alone does THREE of them (Genitive, Locative, and the virile Accusative that landed one node ago). The adjective itself carries NO information about which job it is in - the trigger word in front and the noun behind it are the only evidence. That is a case-ending cliff by the rule's own definition, and a same-string-many-jobs collision is precisely what massed discrimination is for. This is the ONLY new gym in C1 besides the c1_case_gym closer; every other C1 system recycles through later units' sentences, which the rule names as the default mechanism.

SLIDE 3 IS THE GYM'S ONE GENUINELY NEW THOUGHT, and it is a load-REDUCING one rather than a new fact: of the six jobs, THE MEN/NOT-MEN SPLIT SHOWS IN ONLY TWO - the subject form (dobre filmy / dobrzy studenci) and the object form (dobre filmy / dobrych studentow). In all four oblique jobs - after duzo and nie ma, after w/na/o, after z, after pomagac and dziekowac - the plural adjective is ONE FORM FOR EVERYONE. Each of the four oblique units said this about itself in isolation (c1_adj_pl_inst: 'the Instrumental plural has no virile split'; c1_adj_pl_dat: 'the Dative plural has no virile split either'); no unit has yet been able to say it about the whole block, because c1_adj_pl_virile only landed one node ago. Saying it once, here, is worth more than the four separate reassurances were.

duzy's PARADIGM HOLE IS INHERITED, NOT FIXED, exactly as c1_adj_pl_inst and c1_adj_pl_dat predicted it would be. duzy has duzych (Genitive and Locative plural) and NOTHING ELSE OBLIQUE anywhere in the course - duzymi, duzym, duzego, duzej are all verified NEW - because b2_adj_gen, b2_adj_loc and b2_adj_dat each dropped duzy from their sets and c1_adj_pl_inst could not place it against eleven person nouns. So duzy appears here ONLY in Genitive and Locative slots, and quiz item 9's distractor set is built from duze / duzo / duza rather than from the -ymi and -ym forms the other three adjectives supply. THE GYM IS THE PLACE C1-SPINE'S O-list SAID THE HOLE COULD BE CLOSED and it is deliberately NOT closed here, because closing it would mean teaching new forms in a zero-new gym. Still James's call, restated in the digest.

NO VIRILE LOCATIVE ANYWHERE, and that is lexical rather than editorial: lekarzach and studentach are both verified NEW (b2_loc_pl's eleven nouns are all things), so every Locative slot in the file takes a non-person noun. The virile split is therefore demonstrated on the Nominative and Accusative, where it actually shows, and the Locative rows carry the no-split half of slide 3's claim.

THE QUIZ IS BUILT SO THAT ALL TWELVE ANSWERS ARE DISTINCT, which took real work in a gym whose whole point is that one string answers to three different triggers - the naive board would have had dobrych as the answer three times over. The collision is preserved where it matters by keeping the CHOICE SETS identical across items 1, 3 and 10 (dobrych / dobrymi / dobrym / dobre, reordered) while the answers differ, so the learner meets the same four buttons under three different trigger words. Items 2, 5, 9 and 11 rotate the adjective instead of the ending for the same reason.

ITEM 12 IS THE WOMEN-ONLY GUARD, carried forward from c1_adj_pl_virile one node back, because the predictable error after a men-group unit is to read the category as 'people' rather than 'masculine-personal'. Corki sa zmeczone is the sentence that says otherwise, and it is the same guard b2_num_virile built its feminine defence around (osoba is feminine, so piec osob and never pieciu).

FENCED: mali, duzi, dzieciach, lekarzach, studentach, starych, zimnych, stare, mlode, wszyscy - all verified NEW and appearing nowhere, including as distractors. -ich (wysokich, drogich) is out; every adjective in the block is a hard stem. ci is used in its b1_virile_reco job only (the virile nominative demonstrative); the b1_dative_pron clitic sense appears nowhere and no dative pronoun construction is used anywhere in the file. oni/one sit in the auditor's GLUE_LEMMAS where it cannot see them and are used NOWHERE - every sentence names its subject with a noun.

PISANIE: twelve items, every one a two- or three-word pattern phrase and all twelve distinct under the engine's own norm(). The prepositional cases type their governor (w nowych sklepach, z dobrymi kolegami - the w domu shape AGENTS names, since neither case exists without it); the Genitive types its quantity word (duzo dobrych filmow); the Dative and both Nominative/Accusative jobs type adjective + noun alone, because there the governor is a verb and does not belong inside the minimal pattern unit. Under the 3-word cap, pattern phrases and not composed sentences; nothing added to the repair queue.

TITLE: the planned tree label read 'Silownia - dobre i dobrych' and every word of it is taught, so unlike the previous three nodes this one did not have to be rescued. It was sharpened rather than corrected, to 'Silownia - dobrych, dobrymi, dobrym', which names the three-string collision the gym exists for; all three forms are owned, and check_new.py was re-run on every word at the wire per C1-SPINE's build protocol.

intro.title: One adjective, six jobs
intro.body: Every plural adjective ending this course teaches, on one board. The adjective never tells you which job it is in. The word in front of it does.

rows: Filmy są dobre. Studenci są dobrzy.

intro.title: -ych does three jobs. Read the word in front.
intro.body: Three of the six jobs are the same four letters. There is nothing inside -ych that says which one you are looking at, and there never will be. The trigger word settles it every time, and the noun behind confirms it.

intro.title: The men/not-men split shows in only two of the six
intro.body: This is the part worth keeping. A group with a man in it takes a special adjective when it is the subject, and again when it is the object. In the other four jobs — after dużo, after w, na and o, after z, after pomagać and dziękować — the plural adjective is one form for everyone, men or not.

examples.en: In the big cities there are no good shops.
examples.pl: W dużych miastach nie ma dobrych sklepów.

quiz.explain: dużo has taken the Genitive since A1, and the plural adjective there is -ych.
w is a Locative word, and the Locative plural adjective is -ych — the same string dużo takes, doing a different job.
z is the one trigger in the whole board that asks for -ymi. Same four buttons as the last item, different word in front.
pomagać takes the Dative, and -om on the noun confirms it. Read the noun, not the adjective.
An object that is a group with men in it borrows the Genitive, on the noun and on the adjective alike. nowi is the subject form.
studenci is a group with men in it, so ci rather than te — and the adjective after it goes the same way.
Shops are things and this is the subject, so the plain -e plural from A2. Nothing in front of it, nothing borrowed.
The subject is one of the two places where the men/not-men split shows. dobrych would be right the moment this became an object.
nie ma takes the Genitive, exactly as dużo does. dużo is a different word that happens to start the same way, and it can even stand in front: dużo dużych gazet.
dziękować takes the Dative just as pomagać does. The third appearance of these same four buttons, and the third different answer.
z again, so -ymi again — and dziećmi is neuter, which makes no difference at all in the plural.
Worth slowing down for after the last unit. Daughters are people but they are not men, and the special form is about men rather than about people.

type_items.prompt_en: the good students — as the subject
the good students — as the object
type_items.explain: Same two words, and only the job changed. The object form of a men-group plural is the Genitive, borrowed whole.

type_items.prompt_en: the new shops — as the subject
